messages:
From: Alex Torres <contracts@nebulaanalytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulaanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Downstream authority amendment: addition of LogStream Inc. as subprocessor (NB-4872)

Hi Nikhil,

Per section 4.2 of our MSA, Nebula intends to add a new downstream vendor, LogStream Inc. (www.logstream.io), to handle telemetry ingestion and transient storage for our analytics pipeline. This is an addition to the list of subprocessors for the Nebula account (NB-4872).

Summary: 
- Subprocessor: LogStream Inc. (US)
- Purpose: telemetry ingestion, short-term KV cache for traces, non-PII log parsing
- Data types: system logs, anonymized session IDs, event timestamps, telemetry metrics (no raw user content)
- Retention: up to 30 days by default; logs purged after 90 days maximum
- Processing locations: US-only (primary), fallback EU only with prior written consent

Attached: LogStream_delegation_notice.pdf; LogStream_SOW_summary.pdf

Request: per our MSA we are providing this notice and requesting Redwood's written consent (or a reasonable objection) within 10 business days. Also please confirm any evidence you require (SOC 2 report, DPA addendum signed by LogStream, encryption-in-transit attestations).

Contact at LogStream: Jamie Park <jamie.park@logstream.io> (ops lead).

Happy to hop on a short call if helpful — proposed availability Mon/Tue morning PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Torres

contracts@nebulaanalytics.com

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the initial materials — a few items we require before providing written consent: 

1) Evidence pack from LogStream (preferably straight from Nebula or LogStream): SOC 2 Type II report (latest), completed vendor security questionnaire, and a signed DPA/addendum binding LogStream to Nebula's DPA obligations.

2) Confirmation on data categories: you note "no raw user content" — we need Nebula to confirm in writing that no user-provided text or PII will be routed to LogStream. If there is any chance of content data (chat, transcripts) being included, we must reject or require additional controls.

3) Processing geography hard stop: because Nebula said primary is US-only, we need a contractual assurance restricting EU processing unless we agree in writing. If LogStream will have EU fallback, include the fallback triggers and documentation of safeguards (e.g., SCCs, EU DPA clause).

4) Security controls: TLS 1.2+ in transit, at-rest encryption details for the 30–90 day retention window, RBAC/limited access logs, and Azure/AWS account boundaries if used.

5) Evidence delivery: ask that Nebula provide the evidence bundle to legal@redwood.com and include a short statement of scope (what Nebula is sending to LogStream). We'll use that to run a quick vendor risk check.

Temporary mitigation: we can provisionally allow non-PII telemetry ingestion for 30 days pending receipt of SOC2/DPA, provided LogStream signs our standard addendum via DocuSign and we receive encryption attestations. Full consent will be contingent on the evidence pack.

I've attached a short checklist you can send to Nebula to expedite: evidence_checklist.csv

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachment: evidence_checklist.csv (CSV)

Alex — thanks for the notice and materials. We reviewed and can provide provisional consent with the following conditions: 

1) Nebula or LogStream must deliver the evidence pack (SOC 2 Type II, completed security questionnaire, and signed DPA addendum via DocuSign) to legal@redwood.com within 10 business days. DocuSign link (preferred): https://www.docusign.net/DocuSign/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=1111&v=5

2) Processing allowed is limited to non-PII telemetry (system logs, anonymized session ids, event timestamps, metrics). Any user-generated content, customer chat, or identifiable personal data is explicitly excluded unless we execute an amended agreement covering those categories.

3) Processing in EU: Not permitted without a separate written approval from Redwood legal documenting SCCs and any necessary DPA amendments.

4) Retention and encryption attestations: please confirm at-rest encryption and time-bound retention policies (30–90 days) in writing.

If Nebula provides the required artifacts within 10 business days, we will update this thread with final written consent. If items are missing, we will escalate to procurement/legal for triage and may require a temporary block.

Happy to join a quick call with Jamie Park (LogStream) if that helps speed things up — availability Tues/Wed 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
